Eiffel_Tower.name: Eiffel Tower
Eiffel_Tower.historical_background: Constructed for the 1889 World's Fair, it was initially criticized but became a global cultural icon.
interesting_facts: The tower grows up to 15 cm in summer due to heat expansion.
It was meant to be dismantled after 20 years.
It is repainted by hand every 7 years.
Eiffel_Tower.tourist_tips: Book tickets online months in advance to avoid lines.

Taj_Mahal.name: Taj Mahal
Taj_Mahal.historical_background: Built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his favorite wife Mumtaz Mahal.
interesting_facts: It is perfectly symmetrical except for Shah Jahan's tomb.
The colors of the marble change depending on the time of day.
Over 20,000 artisans worked on its construction.
Taj_Mahal.tourist_tips: Visit at sunrise for the best light and fewer crowds.

Colosseum.name: Colosseum
Colosseum.historical_background: The largest ancient amphitheatre ever built, hosting gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.
interesting_facts: It could hold between 50,000 and 80,000 spectators.
Originally known as the Flavian Amphitheatre.
It has been damaged by earthquakes and stone-robbers.
Colosseum.tourist_tips: Buy a combined ticket with the Roman Forum to skip lines.

Pyramids_of_Giza.name: Pyramids of Giza
Pyramids_of_Giza.historical_background: Royal tombs built for three Egyptian pharaohs during the Old Kingdom period.
interesting_facts: The Great Pyramid is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
It was the tallest man-made structure for over 3,800 years.
Constructed using roughly 2.3 million stone blocks.
Pyramids_of_Giza.tourist_tips: Wear comfortable shoes and carry plenty of water.

Statue_of_Liberty.name: Statue of Liberty
Statue_of_Liberty.historical_background: A gift from the people of France to the United States to celebrate freedom and democracy.
interesting_facts: The green color is due to the natural weathering of copper.
The statue represents Libertas, the Roman goddess of liberty.
The torch was originally used as a lighthouse beacon.
Statue_of_Liberty.tourist_tips: Book crown access tickets several months in advance.

Machu_Picchu.name: Machu Picchu
Machu_Picchu.historical_background: An Inca citadel set high in the Andes mountains, abandoned and later rediscovered in 1911.
interesting_facts: Built without using wheels, mortar, or draft animals.
The stones are cut so precisely that a knife blade cannot fit between them.
It serves as an astronomical observatory.
Machu_Picchu.tourist_tips: Acclimatize in Cusco for a few days to avoid altitude sickness.

Great_Wall_of_China.name: Great Wall of China
Great_Wall_of_China.historical_background: A vast series of fortifications built across historical northern borders to protect against invasions.
interesting_facts: Contrary to myth, it is not easily visible from space without magnification.
It is the longest man-made structure in the world.
Glutinous rice flour was used in the mortar for stability.
Great_Wall_of_China.tourist_tips: Visit the Mutianyu or Jinshanling sections to avoid massive tourist crowds.

Sydney_Opera_House.name: Sydney Opera House
Sydney_Opera_House.historical_background: A world-renowned performing arts centre famed for its iconic sail-like roof structure.
interesting_facts: The sails are covered in over 1 million self-cleaning Swedish tiles.
The architect resigned before construction was completed.
It has its own concert hall organ, the largest mechanical action organ in the world.
Sydney_Opera_House.best_time_to_visit: March to May (Autumn) or September to November (Spring)
Sydney_Opera_House.entry_fee: Free to walk around; tours start at AUD $43
Sydney_Opera_House.tourist_tips: Take a guided tour to access the interior concert halls and learn its history.

Stonehenge.name: Stonehenge
Stonehenge.historical_background: A prehistoric monument consisting of an outer ring of vertical sarsen standing stones.
interesting_facts: The bluestones were transported from Wales, over 150 miles away.
It is aligned with the sunrise on the summer solstice.
Its exact purpose remains one of history's greatest mysteries.
Stonehenge.best_time_to_visit: June (for Solstice) or late Spring/early Autumn
Stonehenge.tourist_tips: Pre-book tickets online. It is often very windy, so dress warmly.

Christ_the_Redeemer.name: Christ the Redeemer
Christ_the_Redeemer.architect: Heitor da Silva Costa, Paul Landowski (Sculptor)
Christ_the_Redeemer.unesco_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (as part of Rio, 2012)
Christ_the_Redeemer.historical_background: A massive soapstone statue of Jesus Christ overlooking Rio de Janeiro from Mount Corcovado.
interesting_facts: It is the largest Art Deco-style statue in the world.
The outer layers are made of thousands of triangular soapstone tiles.
It is frequently struck by lightning during storms.
Christ_the_Redeemer.best_time_to_visit: September to November or March to May
Christ_the_Redeemer.tourist_tips: Take the Cog Train through the Tijuca Rainforest to reach the top.

Golden_Gate_Bridge.name: Golden Gate Bridge
Golden_Gate_Bridge.architect: Joseph Strauss, Irving Morrow, Charles Ellis
Golden_Gate_Bridge.historical_background: Spanning the Golden Gate strait, it connects San Francisco to Marin County.
interesting_facts: The unique color is called International Orange, chosen for visibility in heavy fog.
It was the longest suspension bridge main span in the world until 1964.
It contains enough cable wire to circle the Earth three times.
Golden_Gate_Bridge.entry_fee: Free for pedestrians/cyclists; Toll for southbound cars (~$9)
Golden_Gate_Bridge.tourist_tips: Walk or bike across from the South Vista Point for the best photo ops.

Burj_Khalifa.name: Burj Khalifa
Burj_Khalifa.historical_background: The tallest building and tallest free-standing structure in the world, symbolizing Dubai's global status.
interesting_facts: It stands at an incredible height of 828 meters (2,717 feet).
The design is inspired by the Hymenocallis, a desert flower.
It holds the record for the highest outdoor observation deck.
Burj_Khalifa.entry_fee: AED 169 to AED 553 (varies by deck level and time)
Burj_Khalifa.opening_hours: 24/7 for residents; Observation decks open 08:30 AM - Midnight
Burj_Khalifa.tourist_tips: Book 'At the Top' tickets in advance to secure sunset slots.

India_Gate.name: India Gate
India_Gate.historical_background: A war memorial dedicated to British Indian Army soldiers who died in World War I.
interesting_facts: The names of over 13,000 soldiers are inscribed on the walls.
Features the Amar Jawan Jyoti (Flame of the Immortal Soldier) underneath the arch.
Inspired by the Arc de Triomphe in Paris.
India_Gate.tourist_tips: Visit in the evening when it is beautifully illuminated.

Gateway_of_India.name: Gateway of India
Gateway_of_India.historical_background: Built to commemorate the landing of King George V and Queen Mary in India in 1911.
interesting_facts: It served as the ceremonial entrance to India for British viceroys.
The last British troops left India through this arch in 1948.
Overlooks the Arabian Sea.
Gateway_of_India.tourist_tips: Take a ferry from the gateway to Elephanta Caves.

Red_Fort.name: Red Fort
Red_Fort.historical_background: Constructed by Shah Jahan when he shifted the Mughal capital from Agra to Delhi.
interesting_facts: Made of massive red sandstone walls.
The Prime Minister of India unfurls the national flag here on Independence Day.
It once housed the famous Koh-i-Noor diamond in the Peacock Throne.
Red_Fort.tourist_tips: Hire an official guide at the entrance to understand the history of the chambers.

Qutub_Minar.name: Qutub Minar
Qutub_Minar.historical_background: A 73-meter tall minaret representing victory and Indo-Islamic building prowess.
interesting_facts: It is the tallest brick minaret in the world.
The complex contains a famous rust-resistant iron pillar from the 4th century.
It features five distinct stories decorated with delicate carvings.
Qutub_Minar.tourist_tips: Check out the nearby unfinished Alai Minar, intended to be twice the height.

Lotus_Temple.name: Lotus Temple
Lotus_Temple.historical_background: A Bahá'í House of Worship notable for its flowerlike shape open to all religions.
interesting_facts: Constructed using 27 free-standing marble petals.
The temple has won numerous architectural awards.
One of the most visited buildings in the world, attracting millions annually.
Lotus_Temple.tourist_tips: Silence must be maintained inside the prayer hall at all times.

Charminar.name: Charminar
Charminar.historical_background: Built to celebrate the end of a deadly plague in the city of Hyderabad.
interesting_facts: The name translates to 'Four Minarets'.
Features a mosque on its top floor.
Located at the intersection of historic trade routes.
Charminar.tourist_tips: Visit the bustling Lad Bazar nearby for traditional pearl and bangle shopping.

Mysore_Palace.name: Mysore Palace
Mysore_Palace.historical_background: Official residence of the Wadiyar dynasty, who ruled Mysore state.
interesting_facts: One of the most famous tourist attractions in India after the Taj Mahal.
Illuminated by nearly 100,000 lightbulbs on Sundays and holidays.
It replaces an older wooden palace that burnt down in 1897.
Mysore_Palace.best_time_to_visit: October to March (especially during Dasara festival)
Mysore_Palace.tourist_tips: Do not miss the light and sound show held in the evening.

Hawa_Mahal.name: Hawa Mahal
Hawa_Mahal.unesco_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (as part of Jaipur, 2019)
Hawa_Mahal.historical_background: Built to allow royal women to observe street festivals without being seen by the public.
interesting_facts: The name translates to 'Palace of Winds'.
Features 953 small windows (jharokhas) decorated with intricate latticework.
Constructed using pink and red sandstone.
Hawa_Mahal.tourist_tips: The front facade is best photographed from the cafes across the street.

Konark_Sun_Temple.name: Konark Sun Temple
Konark_Sun_Temple.historical_background: A temple built in the shape of a monumental chariot dedicated to the Sun God Surya.
interesting_facts: Features 24 stone-carved wheels, which act as accurate sundials.
Originally stood right on the shoreline of the Bay of Bengal.
Often referred to as the 'Black Pagoda'.
Konark_Sun_Temple.tourist_tips: Hire a guide to explain the astronomical significance of the wheel carvings.

Victoria_Memorial.name: Victoria Memorial
Victoria_Memorial.historical_background: Built in memory of Queen Victoria, it now serves as a museum and tourist landmark.
interesting_facts: Constructed using white Makrana marble, the same marble used for the Taj Mahal.
The gardens cover 64 acres of land.
Features a bronze Angel of Victory atop the central dome.
Victoria_Memorial.tourist_tips: Spend time exploring the royal gallery paintings inside.

Gol_Gumbaz.name: Gol Gumbaz
Gol_Gumbaz.historical_background: Mausoleum of King Muhammad Adil Shah of the Adil Shahi dynasty.
interesting_facts: Features the second largest dome in the world after St. Peter's Basilica.
Contains a 'Whispering Gallery' where even the softest sound is echoed eleven times.
Constructed without any central pillars.
Gol_Gumbaz.tourist_tips: Arrive early to visit the Whispering Gallery before it gets too noisy.

Brihadeeswarar_Temple.name: Brihadeeswarar Temple
Brihadeeswarar_Temple.unesco_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (as part of Great Living Chola Temples, 1987)
Brihadeeswarar_Temple.historical_background: A monumental Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva, exemplifying Chola architectural greatness.
interesting_facts: The temple tower (Vimana) is 66 meters high.
The top stone (Kumbam) is carved from a single granite block weighing 80 tons.
Features a massive monolithic statue of Nandi (the sacred bull) at the entrance.
Brihadeeswarar_Temple.tourist_tips: Look for the detailed ancient Tamil inscriptions carved into the temple base.

Sanchi_Stupa.name: Sanchi Stupa
Sanchi_Stupa.historical_background: One of the oldest stone structures in India, built to house relics of the Buddha.
interesting_facts: The gateways (toranas) depict scenes from the Jataka tales of Buddha's life.
It is featured on the reverse side of the Indian 200 rupee note.
Survived centuries of neglect before restoration in the early 20th century.
Sanchi_Stupa.tourist_tips: Spend time examining the beautiful carvings on the four decorative gateways.

Ajanta_Caves.name: Ajanta Caves
Ajanta_Caves.historical_background: A collection of 30 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments famous for ancient masterpieces of painting.
interesting_facts: The caves were lost for centuries before being rediscovered by a British officer hunting tigers in 1819.
The murals are considered masterpieces of Buddhist religious art.
Carved into a horseshoe-shaped cliff side along the Waghur river.
Ajanta_Caves.tourist_tips: Bring a flashlight as many of the cave interiors are dimly lit to preserve the paintings.

Ellora_Caves.name: Ellora Caves
Ellora_Caves.architectural_style: Rock-cut Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain Caves
Ellora_Caves.historical_background: A complex of 34 rock-cut temples representing religious harmony in ancient India.
interesting_facts: Features the Kailash Temple, the largest single monolithic rock excavation in the world.
The Kailash temple was carved from the top down.
Features caves dedicated to three major religions: Buddhism, Hinduism, and Jainism.
Ellora_Caves.tourist_tips: Cave 16 (Kailash Temple) requires at least 2 hours to explore fully.

Humayuns_Tomb.name: Humayun's Tomb
Humayuns_Tomb.historical_background: Commissioned by Humayun's first wife Empress Bega Begum, it was the first garden-tomb in India.
interesting_facts: It inspired the architectural design of the Taj Mahal.
Built using red sandstone and white marble.
It sits within a large charbagh (four-quadrant garden) complex.
Humayuns_Tomb.tourist_tips: Visit in the late afternoon to catch the golden sunlight hitting the red sandstone.

Meenakshi_Temple.name: Meenakshi Temple
Meenakshi_Temple.historical_background: A historic Hindu temple complex dedicated to Meenakshi (a form of Parvati) and Sundareswarar (Shiva).
interesting_facts: Features 14 gateway towers (gopurams), the tallest of which is 52 meters high.
The temple is covered in thousands of colorful stone figures of gods and demons.
Features a Hall of Thousand Pillars, where each pillar is intricately carved.
Meenakshi_Temple.tourist_tips: Be aware of strict dress codes (legs and shoulders must be covered).

Golden_Temple.name: Golden Temple
Golden_Temple.historical_background: Also known as Sri Harmandir Sahib, it is the spiritual focal point and holiest shrine of Sikhism.
interesting_facts: The upper dome is covered with 750 kg of pure gold leaf.
Houses the Guru Ka Langar, a kitchen serving free hot meals to over 100,000 people daily regardless of faith.
Surrounded by a sacred pool called the Amrit Sarovar.
Golden_Temple.tourist_tips: Cover your head with a scarf and wash your feet at the entrance pool before entering.

Nalanda_Ruins.name: Nalanda Ruins
Nalanda_Ruins.historical_background: An ancient university and Buddhist monastery that was a renowned center of learning.
interesting_facts: Widely considered the first residential university in the world.
Had a massive library containing millions of books, which allegedly burnt for months when sacked.
Attracted scholars from China, Korea, Tibet, and Central Asia.
Nalanda_Ruins.tourist_tips: Visit the nearby Nalanda Archaeological Museum for well-preserved sculptures and sealings.

Forbidden_City.name: Forbidden City
Forbidden_City.historical_background: The former Chinese imperial palace from the Ming dynasty to the end of the Qing dynasty.
interesting_facts: It consists of 980 surviving buildings and historically 9,999 rooms.
Served as the home of 24 Chinese emperors.
The walls are made of clay and sticky rice mortar.
Forbidden_City.tourist_tips: Passport or ID is required for entry; buy tickets online in advance.

Mount_Fuji.name: Mount Fuji
Mount_Fuji.historical_background: Japan's tallest mountain and an active volcano, long revered as a sacred site of artistic inspiration.
interesting_facts: It has an exceptionally symmetrical cone shape.
It is one of Japan's 'Three Holy Mountains'.
The climbing season is very short, running from July to early September.
Mount_Fuji.best_time_to_visit: July to August (for climbing) or Winter (for snow-capped photography)
Mount_Fuji.tourist_tips: Lake Kawaguchiko offers some of the most iconic postcard views of the mountain.

Angkor_Wat.name: Angkor Wat
Angkor_Wat.historical_background: Originally constructed as a Hindu temple for the god Vishnu, it gradually transformed into a Buddhist temple.
interesting_facts: It is the largest religious monument in the world by land area.
It is depicted on Cambodia's national flag.
Oriented towards the west, which is unusual for Hindu temples.
Angkor_Wat.tourist_tips: Arrive at 5:00 AM to see the sunrise reflect in the lily ponds.

Petronas_Twin_Towers.name: Petronas Twin Towers
Petronas_Twin_Towers.historical_background: Twin skyscrapers that were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004.
interesting_facts: They remain the tallest twin towers in the world.
Features a double-decker skybridge connecting the towers on the 41st and 42nd floors.
The design reflects Islamic architecture concepts like the Rub el Hizb.
Petronas_Twin_Towers.best_time_to_visit: December to February or June to August
Petronas_Twin_Towers.tourist_tips: Buy tickets online ahead of time as the daily visitation slot is capped.

Marina_Bay_Sands.name: Marina Bay Sands
Marina_Bay_Sands.historical_background: An integrated resort fronting Marina Bay, famous for its boat-shaped cantilevered sky park.
interesting_facts: Features the world's longest elevated infinity swimming pool.
It is one of the most expensive standalone casino properties in the world.
The SkyPark is long enough to park four and a half A380 jumbo jets.
Marina_Bay_Sands.entry_fee: Free for hotel guests; Observation deck ticket starts at SGD $26
Marina_Bay_Sands.tourist_tips: The infinity pool is strictly exclusive to hotel guests.

Borobudur_Temple.name: Borobudur Temple
Borobudur_Temple.historical_background: The world's largest Buddhist temple, abandoned in the 14th century and later restored.
interesting_facts: Built with 72 openwork stupas, each containing a statue of Buddha.
Constructed out of volcanic stone blocks without mortar.
Has over 2,600 relief panels depicting Buddhist cosmology.
Borobudur_Temple.tourist_tips: Hire a guide to explain the spiritual meaning behind the carvings on each level.

Shwedagon_Pagoda.name: Shwedagon Pagoda
Shwedagon_Pagoda.historical_background: The most sacred Buddhist pagoda in Myanmar, believed to contain relics of four Buddhas.
interesting_facts: The main stupa is plated with actual gold bars.
The crown is tipped with 5,448 diamonds and 2,317 rubies.
It is also known as the Great Dagon Pagoda.
Shwedagon_Pagoda.tourist_tips: Dress respectfully; knees and shoulders must be covered. You must enter barefoot.

Taipei_101.name: Taipei 101
Taipei_101.historical_background: A landmark supertall skyscraper that was the world's tallest building until 2010.
interesting_facts: Features a giant 660-tonne steel pendulum damper that stabilizes it during typhoons.
Its sections are designed to resemble stalks of bamboo.
Has some of the world's fastest passenger elevators.
Taipei_101.tourist_tips: Go to the 89th floor to view the giant wind damper in person.

Gyeongbokgung_Palace.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
Gyeongbokgung_Palace.historical_background: The main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty, serving as the seat of government.
interesting_facts: Its name translates to 'Palace Greatly Blessed by Heaven'.
Largely destroyed during the Japanese invasions and rebuilt in the 19th century.
Hosts the famous Royal Guard Changing Ceremony.
Gyeongbokgung_Palace.tourist_tips: Rent a traditional Korean Hanbok nearby for free entry and great photos.

Big_Ben.name: Big Ben
Big_Ben.unesco_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (as part of Palace of Westminster, 1987)
Big_Ben.historical_background: The clock tower of the Palace of Westminster, officially renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012.
interesting_facts: Big Ben is actually the nickname for the giant bell inside, not the tower itself.
The tower leans slightly to the northwest.
The clock face features Latin inscription: 'Domine Salvam Fac Reginam Nostram Victoriam Primam'.
Big_Ben.entry_fee: Free to view; Tours for UK residents require booking via MP
Big_Ben.tourist_tips: Westminster Bridge is the best vantage point for taking photos.

Leaning_Tower_of_Pisa.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
Leaning_Tower_of_Pisa.historical_background: The freestanding bell tower of Pisa Cathedral, famous for its unintended tilt.
interesting_facts: The lean began during construction due to soft ground and poor foundations.
It leans at an angle of about 3.97 degrees.
Engineers stabilized the tower in the 1990s to prevent collapse.
Leaning_Tower_of_Pisa.tourist_tips: Climbing requires booking a timed ticket online. Expect high queues for photo poses.

Arc_de_Triomphe.name: Arc de Triomphe
Arc_de_Triomphe.historical_background: Built to honor those who fought and died for France in the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars.
interesting_facts: Stands at the center of the Place Charles de Gaulle, where 12 avenues meet.
Beneath its vault lies the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier from WWI.
The names of French victories and generals are inscribed on the walls.
Arc_de_Triomphe.tourist_tips: Do NOT try to cross the massive roundabout on foot; use the pedestrian underground tunnels instead.

Louvre_Museum.name: Louvre Museum
Louvre_Museum.architect: Pierre Lescot (original palace), I.M. Pei (Glass Pyramid)
Louvre_Museum.historical_background: The world's largest art museum, housed in the historic Louvre Palace.
interesting_facts: Housed the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and Winged Victory.
It would take 100 days to see every piece of art if you spent 30 seconds on each.
Originally built as a fortress in the 12th century.
Louvre_Museum.tourist_tips: Book a timed entry online. Use the Carrousel du Louvre underground entrance to avoid the long pyramid lines.

Notre_Dame_Cathedral.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
Notre_Dame_Cathedral.historical_background: An iconic medieval cathedral famous for its pioneering flying buttresses and stained-glass rose windows.
interesting_facts: Suffered a catastrophic fire in 2019 that destroyed its spire and roof.
The cathedral is the setting for Victor Hugo's novel 'The Hunchback of Notre-Dame'.
Features famous gargoyles and chimeras on its towers.
Notre_Dame_Cathedral.entry_fee: Free (temporarily closed to public for post-fire restoration)
Notre_Dame_Cathedral.tourist_tips: Check the progress of the rebuilding from the Pont de l'Archevêché.

Tower_Bridge.name: Tower Bridge
Tower_Bridge.historical_background: A combined bascule and suspension bridge crossing the River Thames near the Tower of London.
interesting_facts: The bridge lifts (bascules) are raised about 1,000 times a year to let ships pass.
Features high-level glass-floor walkways with views of the river.
Historically run by steam engines, now powered by electro-hydraulics.
Tower_Bridge.entry_fee: Free to walk across; Exhibition/walkway ticket is £11.40
Tower_Bridge.tourist_tips: Check the lift schedule online to see the bridge lift in action.

Buckingham_Palace.name: Buckingham Palace
Buckingham_Palace.historical_background: The official London residence and administrative headquarters of the British monarch.
interesting_facts: Features 775 rooms, including 19 State Rooms.
If the Royal Standard flag is flying, the monarch is in residence; if the Union Jack is flying, they are not.
Hosts the famous Changing of the Guard ceremony.
Buckingham_Palace.best_time_to_visit: Summer (July to September for State Room openings)
Buckingham_Palace.entry_fee: Free to view exterior; State Room tickets are ~£30
Buckingham_Palace.opening_hours: Exterior view 24/7; Changing of the Guard is 11:00 AM on select days
Buckingham_Palace.tourist_tips: Arrive early for the Changing of the Guard to secure a spot near the gates.

Acropolis_of_Athens.name: Acropolis of Athens
Acropolis_of_Athens.historical_background: An ancient citadel located on a rocky outcrop containing the Parthenon and other temples.
interesting_facts: The Parthenon was built to honor the goddess Athena.
Features the Caryatids, statues of female figures serving as architectural columns.
Damaged by a Venetian mortar strike in 1687 during a siege.
Acropolis_of_Athens.tourist_tips: Arrive at 8:00 AM sharp to beat the cruise ship crowds and intense midday heat.

Empire_State_Building.name: Empire State Building
Empire_State_Building.historical_background: A 102-story Art Deco skyscraper in Midtown Manhattan that was the tallest building for 40 years.
interesting_facts: Completed in just 410 days during the Great Depression.
Its spire was originally designed to be a mooring mast for airships.
The tower lights change colors to celebrate different holidays.
Empire_State_Building.entry_fee: USD $44 to $79 depending on observation decks
Empire_State_Building.tourist_tips: Go late at night (after 10 PM) or early morning to avoid crowd wait times.

White_House.name: White House
White_House.historical_background: The official residence and workplace of the President of the United States.
interesting_facts: Burnt down by British forces in 1814 and subsequently rebuilt.
The West Wing was added by President Theodore Roosevelt.
Features 132 rooms and 35 bathrooms.
White_House.entry_fee: Free (Requires tour booking months in advance through embassy/congressperson)
White_House.tourist_tips: Public tours must be submitted up to 3 months in advance.

Mount_Rushmore.name: Mount Rushmore
Mount_Rushmore.historical_background: A colossal sculpture carved into the Black Hills of South Dakota depicting four US Presidents.
interesting_facts: Depicts Presidents George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt, and Abraham Lincoln.
The heads are approximately 60 feet tall.
Originally intended to carve the presidents from the waist up.
Mount_Rushmore.tourist_tips: Visit during the evening for the lighting ceremony.

Space_Needle.name: Space Needle
Space_Needle.architect: Edward E. Carlson, John Graham Jr.
Space_Needle.historical_background: Built as the centerpiece of the 1962 World's Fair, symbolizing Seattle's futuristic outlook.
interesting_facts: Features the world's first revolving glass floor ('The Loupe').
Can withstand earthquakes of up to 9.0 magnitude.
The design represents a flying saucer on a slender tower.
Space_Needle.tourist_tips: Buy a combined ticket with Chihuly Garden and Glass next door to save money.

CN_Tower.name: CN Tower
CN_Tower.historical_background: A signature icon of Toronto's skyline, built by Canadian National railway company.
interesting_facts: Stands at 553.3 meters (1,815 feet) tall.
Was the world's tallest free-standing structure until 2007.
Offers the 'EdgeWalk', a hands-free walk on a ledge around the tower's main pod.
CN_Tower.tourist_tips: Try the famous Glass Floor, where you can look straight down to the street level.

Chichen_Itza.name: Chichen Itza
Chichen_Itza.historical_background: A large pre-Columbian city built by the Maya people, famous for the El Castillo pyramid.
interesting_facts: El Castillo has 365 steps, representing the days of the solar year.
During equinoxes, the shadow of the pyramid creates the illusion of a snake crawling down.
Climbing the pyramid was banned in 2006 for preservation.
Chichen_Itza.tourist_tips: Arrive early before tour buses from Cancún arrive around 10:30 AM.

Iguazu_Falls.name: Iguazu Falls
Iguazu_Falls.historical_background: The largest waterfall system in the world, straddling the border between Argentina and Brazil.
interesting_facts: Consists of approximately 275 individual drops.
The most famous section is called the Devil's Throat (Garganta del Diablo).
Eleanor Roosevelt reportedly exclaimed 'Poor Niagara!' upon seeing them.
Iguazu_Falls.best_time_to_visit: April to June or August to October
Iguazu_Falls.tourist_tips: Visit both sides: the Argentine side gets you close, the Brazilian side gives panoramic views.

Moai_Statues.name: Moai Statues
Moai_Statues.unesco_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (as part of Rapa Nui National Park, 1995)
Moai_Statues.historical_background: Monolithic human figures carved by the Rapa Nui people, representing deified ancestors.
interesting_facts: There are nearly 1,000 statues scattered across the island.
Most are carved from volcanic tuff from the Rano Raraku quarry.
They have full bodies underground, though only the heads are commonly seen.
Moai_Statues.tourist_tips: Do not touch the statues under any circumstances, as they are sacred.

Sheikh_Zayed_Grand_Mosque.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
Sheikh_Zayed_Grand_Mosque.historical_background: The largest mosque in the UAE, built to represent Islamic architectural heritage.
interesting_facts: Houses the world's largest hand-knotted carpet in the main prayer hall.
Features 82 domes and 24-carat gold-plated chandeliers.
It can accommodate over 40,000 worshippers.
Sheikh_Zayed_Grand_Mosque.opening_hours: 09:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily (Closed to tourists Fri morning)
Sheikh_Zayed_Grand_Mosque.tourist_tips: Strict dress codes are enforced; women must wear an abaya (provided for free).

Petra.name: Petra
Petra.historical_background: An ancient city carved directly into vibrant rose-red sandstone cliffs, serving as the Nabataean capital.
interesting_facts: Known as the 'Rose City' due to the color of the stone.
Accessed through a narrow canyon called the Siq.
The most famous monument is Al-Khazneh (The Treasury).
Petra.best_time_to_visit: March to May or September to November
Petra.tourist_tips: Buy the Jordan Pass before arriving to save on visa and entry fees.

Dome_of_the_Rock.name: Dome of the Rock
Dome_of_the_Rock.architect: Raja ibn Haywah, Yazid ibn Salam
Dome_of_the_Rock.historical_background: An Islamic shrine situated on the Temple Mount, one of the oldest extant works of Islamic architecture.
interesting_facts: The dome is covered in 80 kg of pure gold leaf.
It sits over the Foundation Stone, sacred to Muslims, Jews, and Christians.
Its octagonal structure is modeled after Byzantine churches.
Dome_of_the_Rock.entry_fee: Free (non-Muslims cannot enter the dome itself)
Dome_of_the_Rock.opening_hours: Temple Mount grounds open for limited hours Mon-Thu
Dome_of_the_Rock.tourist_tips: Dress highly conservatively; carry no religious items of other faiths.

Great_Sphinx.name: Great Sphinx
Great_Sphinx.historical_background: A colossal statue of a mythical creature with the body of a lion and the head of a human.
interesting_facts: It is the oldest known monumental sculpture in Egypt.
Carved out of a single ridge of limestone bedrock.
The nose was lost historically before the Napoleonic era.
Great_Sphinx.tourist_tips: Walk down the causeway of Khafre's pyramid to get the best closeup photos.

Table_Mountain.name: Table Mountain
Table_Mountain.unesco_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Cape Floral Region)
Table_Mountain.historical_background: A prominent flat-topped mountain forming a landmark overlooking Cape Town.
interesting_facts: It is one of the oldest mountains in the world.
The 'tablecloth' is a cloud formation that frequently covers the flat top.
Home to over 1,500 species of unique plants.
Table_Mountain.entry_fee: Free to hike; Cableway ticket is ~ZAR 400 (~USD $22)
Table_Mountain.tourist_tips: Check the cableway status online before leaving, as it closes due to wind.

Hassan_II_Mosque.name: Hassan II Mosque
Hassan_II_Mosque.historical_background: Built to celebrate King Hassan II's 60th birthday, sitting on a promontory overlooking the Atlantic Ocean.
interesting_facts: Features a 210-meter minaret, one of the tallest in the world.
The mosque features a retractable roof.
Built partly over the Atlantic Ocean, with a glass floor showing the waves below.
Hassan_II_Mosque.best_time_to_visit: March to May or September to November
Hassan_II_Mosque.opening_hours: 09:00 AM - 04:00 PM for guided tour schedules
Hassan_II_Mosque.tourist_tips: It is one of the few active mosques in Morocco open to non-Muslims via guided tours.

Sydney_Harbour_Bridge.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
Sydney_Harbour_Bridge.historical_background: Nicknamed 'The Coathanger', it is a steel arch bridge across Sydney Harbour.
interesting_facts: It is the tallest steel arch bridge in the world.
Features the BridgeClimb, allowing tourists to walk along the top of the arch.
Six million hand-driven rivets were used in its construction.
Sydney_Harbour_Bridge.best_time_to_visit: March to May or September to November
Sydney_Harbour_Bridge.tourist_tips: Take the free pedestrian walkway on the east side for great views of the Opera House.

Uluru.name: Uluru
Uluru.historical_background: A massive sandstone monolith in the Red Centre of Australia, sacred to indigenous Anangu people.
interesting_facts: Also known as Ayers Rock.
It appears to change color at sunrise and sunset, glowing red.
Climbing the rock was permanently banned in 2019 out of respect for its sacred nature.
Uluru.tourist_tips: Do the 10 km base walk to appreciate the scale and caves of the monolith.

Sky_Tower.name: Sky Tower
Sky_Tower.historical_background: A telecommunications and observation tower in Auckland, dominating the skyline.
interesting_facts: Stands at 328 meters (1,076 feet) tall.
It is the tallest man-made structure in New Zealand.
Offers base-jumping simulator ('SkyJump') from the observation deck.
Sky_Tower.tourist_tips: Visit Orbit 360, the revolving restaurant at the top, for panoramic dining.

Neuschwanstein_Castle.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
Neuschwanstein_Castle.historical_background: A 19th-century historicist palace built for King Ludwig II as a personal retreat and homage to Richard Wagner.
interesting_facts: It was the primary inspiration for Disneyland's Sleeping Beauty Castle.
King Ludwig II slept only 11 nights in the castle before his mysterious death.
Despite its medieval look, it had modern systems like running warm water and central heating.
Neuschwanstein_Castle.best_time_to_visit: May to September (warm weather) or Winter (for snow photos)
Neuschwanstein_Castle.tourist_tips: Tickets must be bought online in advance. Walk up to the Marienbrücke bridge for the best postcard view.

Sagrada_Familia.name: Sagrada Família
Sagrada_Familia.historical_background: A large unfinished Roman Catholic minor basilica designed by the famous architect Antoni Gaudí.
interesting_facts: It has been under construction for over 140 years, longer than it took to build the Egyptian pyramids.
Gaudí is buried in the crypt of the basilica.
The towers represent the Twelve Apostles, the Evangelists, the Virgin Mary, and Jesus.
Sagrada_Familia.tourist_tips: Book tickets online 2-3 weeks in advance. Visit in the late afternoon when sunlight streams through the stained-glass windows.

Hagia_Sophia.name: Hagia Sophia
Hagia_Sophia.architect: Isidore of Miletus, Anthemius of Tralles
Hagia_Sophia.unesco_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (as part of Historic Areas of Istanbul, 1985)
Hagia_Sophia.historical_background: Originally built as a Christian cathedral, it later became an Ottoman mosque, a museum, and is currently a mosque again.
interesting_facts: It was the world's largest cathedral for nearly a thousand years.
Features a massive dome that was considered an engineering marvel of antiquity.
Christian mosaics and Islamic calligraphy discs sit side-by-side inside.
Hagia_Sophia.tourist_tips: Dress conservatively (head coverings for women, long pants/skirts for all). Non-Muslim tourists use a separate visitor entrance.

Amer_Fort.name: Amer Fort
Amer_Fort.unesco_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (as part of Hill Forts of Rajasthan, 2013)
Amer_Fort.historical_background: A majestic fort situated on a hill, overlooking Maota Lake, serving as the seat of the Kachwaha clan.
interesting_facts: Famed for its artistic Hindu style elements.
Contains the Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace), decorated with thousands of concave mirrors.
Connected to Jaigarh Fort by a subterranean tunnel.
Amer_Fort.tourist_tips: Enjoy the sound and light show at the fort in the evening.

Hampi_Ruins.name: Hampi Ruins
Hampi_Ruins.historical_background: The capital of the historic Vijayanagara Empire, left in ruins after being sacked in 1565.
interesting_facts: Features the iconic stone chariot temple inside the Vittala Temple complex.
Hampi was the second largest city in the world in the 15th century.
Surrounded by a striking landscape of giant granite boulders.
Hampi_Ruins.tourist_tips: Rent a bicycle or auto-rickshaw to cover the vast ruins spread over 4100 hectares.

Khajuraho_Temples.name: Khajuraho Temples
Khajuraho_Temples.historical_background: A group of Hindu and Jain temples famous for their Nagara-style architectural symbolism and erotic sculptures.
interesting_facts: Originally comprised 85 temples, of which 25 survive today.
Erotic sculptures make up only about 10% of the carvings, depicting life and spiritual union.
Constructed using sandstone block masonry without mortar.
Khajuraho_Temples.tourist_tips: Focus your visit on the Western Group of temples, which contain the most spectacular carvings.

Tokyo_Tower.name: Tokyo Tower
Tokyo_Tower.historical_background: A communication and observation tower that is a beloved landmark of post-war Japan's modern rebirth.
interesting_facts: At 332.9 meters, it is taller than the Eiffel Tower but weighs half as much.
Painted in white and international orange to comply with aviation safety laws.
Features a foot-town amusement building at the base with shops and cafes.
Tokyo_Tower.tourist_tips: Zojo-ji Temple next door is the best spot to capture the tower framed with historic temple gates.

Burj_Al_Arab.name: Burj Al Arab
Burj_Al_Arab.historical_background: An ultra-luxury hotel designed to resemble the billowing sail of a traditional Arabic dhow.
interesting_facts: Stands on an artificial island connected to the mainland by a bridge.
Often described as the world's only '7-star hotel' due to its level of service.
Features a helipad that has hosted famous events like Tiger Woods teeing off.
Burj_Al_Arab.entry_fee: Requires dining booking or guided tour booking (~AED 249) to enter
Burj_Al_Arab.tourist_tips: Jumeirah Public Beach next door offers the best free photo views of the hotel exterior.

Merlion.name: Merlion
Merlion.historical_background: A mythical creature with a lion's head and the body of a fish, serving as Singapore's mascot.
interesting_facts: The fish body represents Singapore's origin as a fishing village (Temasek).
The lion head represents Singapore's original name, Singapura (Lion City).
Spouts water from its mouth into Marina Bay.
Merlion.tourist_tips: Visit at night to see the Merlion lit up and catch the Spectra light and water show across the bay.

Victoria_Falls.name: Victoria Falls
Victoria_Falls.historical_background: One of the world's largest waterfalls, locally known as Mosi-oa-Tunya (The Smoke That Thunders).
interesting_facts: Twice the height of Niagara Falls.
Forms the largest single sheet of flowing water in the world during high river levels.
Features 'Devil's Pool', a natural rock pool right at the edge where tourists can swim in dry season.
Victoria_Falls.best_time_to_visit: February to May (Peak flow) or September to December (Dry season, best for Devil's Pool)
Victoria_Falls.tourist_tips: Wear a waterproof jacket; the spray is so intense it feels like heavy rain and can damage electronic devices.

Blue_Mosque.name: Blue Mosque
Blue_Mosque.unesco_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (as part of Historic Areas of Istanbul, 1985)
Blue_Mosque.historical_background: Also known as the Sultan Ahmed Mosque, famous for its grand scale and blue-tiled interior.
interesting_facts: Nicknamed the 'Blue Mosque' because of the 20,000 hand-painted blue İznik tiles decorating its walls.
It is one of only a few mosques in Turkey with six minarets.
Built directly opposite Hagia Sophia to rival its grandeur.
Blue_Mosque.opening_hours: 08:30 AM - Sunrise (Closed to tourists during daily prayers)
Blue_Mosque.tourist_tips: Avoid visiting during the midday Friday prayers. Women must wear headscarves (borrow at entrance for free).

Kremlin.name: Moscow Kremlin
Kremlin.architect: Italian Architects (commissioned by Ivan the Great)
Kremlin.historical_background: A fortified complex in the heart of Moscow, serving as the official residence of the President of Russia.
interesting_facts: It is the largest active fortress in Europe.
Houses the Tsar Cannon and Tsar Bell, some of the largest in history.
Features five stars made of ruby glass atop the towers, which rotate in the wind.
Kremlin.tourist_tips: Security is extremely high; pass through metal detectors at Kutafiya Tower entrance.

Sydney_Tower.name: Sydney Tower
Sydney_Tower.historical_background: Sydney's tallest structure and the second-tallest observation tower in the Southern Hemisphere.
interesting_facts: Stands at 309 meters tall.
Supported by 56 cables that weigh 7 tons each.
Can withstand extreme earthquakes and high wind speeds.
Sydney_Tower.best_time_to_visit: March to May or September to November
Sydney_Tower.tourist_tips: Do the Skywalk, a high-altitude outdoor tour on a glass-floor viewing platform.

Grand_Palace.name: Grand Palace
Grand_Palace.historical_background: The official ceremonial residence of the Kings of Thailand since 1782.
interesting_facts: Contains the Temple of the Emerald Buddha (Wat Phra Kaew), the most sacred Buddhist temple in Thailand.
Constructed using gold leaf, colorful porcelain mosaics, and carved wood.
Guarded by massive statues of Yaksha (demon guardians).
Grand_Palace.tourist_tips: Strict dress codes apply: no sleeveless shirts, short skirts, shorts, or tight clothing are allowed inside.
